Robert “Bob” Chase, Sr., founder of Quabbin Timber, has died. He was 83.
November 13, 2026 | 12:46 pm CST
Robert “Bob” Chase, Sr., founder of Quabbin Timber, has died. He was 83.
Robert “Bob” Chase of Falmouth, Massachusetts, died on November 7, 2026. He was 83.

Chase, who spent 62 years in the lumber industry, began his career at Guernsey-Westbrook and went on to MacMillan Bloedel and L.R. McCoy. In 1984, he founded Quabbin Timber. Over six decades, he earned a reputation across the industry for his integrity, his knowledge and the lasting relationships he built with customers, suppliers and colleagues. Today, Bob’s legacy lives on through Quabbin Timber.
The Wood Products Manufacturers Association posted a tribute to Chase, praising him for his work in the industry, support of the association, and his impact on the community.

"Bob dedicated 62 years to the lumber industry, earning the respect and friendship of countless colleagues along the way," Michelle Arsenault, executive director, WPMA. "Bob and the Chase family have been valued members and generous supporters of WPMA for many years, contributing their time, leadership, and sponsorship to the Association. "Bob's friendship, wonderful sense of camaraderie, and dedication to our industry will always be remembered. He will be greatly missed by all who had the pleasure of knowing him."

In his obituary, Chase's philanthropic efforts were lauded. "Bob believed in giving back to his community. He served on the Board of Directors of The Goddard House in Worcester and served as President at Briarwood in Worcester, where his leadership and steady judgment were greatly valued. For many years he coached CYO basketball in Walpole. He was a passionate coach, known for his encouragement and love of the game, and many of the young people he coached remember him fondly."

He is survived by his beloved wife of 60 years, Mary E. (Cunneen) Chase; his sons, Robert Chase and his wife, Kimberlee, Stephen Chase and his wife, Maureen, and Brian Chase and Kerrie Lampinen; his cherished grandchildren, Colby, Emily, Kate, Lily, Caroline, Cole and Noah; his sister, Bunny Currie and her husband Jim; and many nieces, nephews and friends.

He was predeceased by his parents, E.A. “Larry” and Mildred Chase; his stepmother, Marion Chase; his daughter-in-law, Amy (Flanagan) Chase, the late wife of Brian; his brother, Tommy MacBeth; his sisters, June Ayer and Marilyn “Mal” Foskett; and his brothers-in-law, Jim Curry and George Foskett.

Larry Adams is a Chicago-based writer and editor who writes about how things get done. A former wire service and community newspaper reporter, Larry is an award-winning writer with more than three decades of experience. In addition to writing about woodworking, he has covered science, metrology, metalworking, industrial design, quality control, imaging, Swiss and micromanufacturing . He was previously a Tabbie Award winner for his coverage of nano-based coatings technology for the automotive industry. Larry volunteers for the historic preservation group, the Kalo Foundation/Ianelli Studios, and the science-based group, Chicago Council on Science and Technology (C2ST).
